You can load up bot lobbies so... what this game really is fun for is just shooting bot gallery for easy kills. It also runs much better than BF6 (Although I still get stutters) and I like how it has some future tech with the time it takes place in.

I do not recommend. If you want a modern Battlefield settings but you can't run BF6, just pick up BF4 instead. It's miles better than this.

Battlefield 2042 is one of the most disappointing Battlefield games I've played. The servers feel almost dead, and it's difficult to find matches with real players since many lobbies are filled with bots, especially outside of peak hours or in less popular modes.

The gameplay still feels clunky at times, and despite years of updates, bugs and glitches are still noticeable. The specialist system also takes away some of the classic Battlefield class identity, and the game lacks the atmosphere and destruction that made older Battlefield titles so memorable.

There have been improvements since launch, but for me they aren't enough to make the game worth its full price. I'd only recommend buying it if it's on a heavy discount and if you're okay with playing against bots, dealing with occasional bugs, and the overall gameplay style.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features AI bots and a solo or co-op mode.

citations.review_text: I’m really happy that I bought this game! I’ve been searching for something like Battlefield 2. BF2042 gives me that feeling of actually being part of a real battlefield. , huge-scale warfare, massive Conquest battles, large maps, and modern military vehicles. The excellent Solo/Co-op AI, the Portal mode! the dynamic atmosphere, and the absolute chaos of the battles are all fantastic. The movement feels perfect, too. I could talk for days about how much I love this game and how amazing everything feels. I’m genuinely thankful to the developers for creating Battlefield 2042. This is exactly the kind of Battlefield experience I’ve been looking for.

One of the best games to play solo with bots or in co-op with friends during some free time on the weekend.

Don’t get me wrong—I used to be a pretty hardcore gamer and was very good at competitive shooters and PvP games back in the day. But time can be cruel. Once I hit 35, I started feeling like I just didn’t have the energy anymore to keep up with the younger generation of PvP players. These days, I’ve gradually shifted toward playing games mainly for fun and relaxation.

Back in the Battlefield 2 days, when I was still playing the game from a physical disc, it already had features that allowed you to host private or solo matches with bots. For me, having that kind of option again is one of the biggest highlights of Battlefield 2042.

When Battlefield 2042 first launched, I honestly couldn’t last more than about 20 minutes before uninstalling it because the game was missing so many things. But in its current state, it’s actually a great experience.

I also hope that maybe six months from now, Battlefield 6 will allow players to create Solo/Co-op matches more freely, because I’d really like to move over to that game eventually. I really enjoy the gameplay of Battlefield 6, but everything feels a little too fast-paced for me. Being forced to join matches with other players, along with the XP limitations when playing against bots, are the main reasons I’ve decided not to choose it for now.

Hopefully DICE updates and improves those features sooner rather than later.

BF2042 is a lot better than it has any right to be, but the player base isn’t there. Lobbies aren’t completely dead, but unless it’s peak hours, half of the lobby will likely be bots and if it’s graveyard hours, there won’t be enough real players to even start a match. Playing against bots isn’t un-fun per say, but it gets boring very quickly so limits the amount of hours you can pump into the game. 

The gun-play is very fluid, the vehicles are well balanced, and the maps are either fun to play, interesting conceptually, or both. Gun-play is far closer to call of duty since there aren't any accuracy penalties for movement, but it still feels like a battlefield game since the map design and vehicles stick close to the battlefield formula and result in a good balance between the two.

Easy to recommend since on sale BF2042 costs practically nothing, but it’s not going to hook you.

Absolutely one of the worst Battlefield games ever made. The game is basically dead—most matches are filled with AI bots because there aren't enough real players. Finding full, active servers is a joke.

On top of that, the optimization is terrible. My CPU would randomly spike in temperature, even hitting 100°C, and the game caused my PC to crash multiple times. No other game on my system does this. Whether it's poor optimization or bad CPU usage, it's unacceptable.

If you're thinking about buying Battlefield 2042, don't. Save your money. If you already bought it and can still refund it, refund this garbage immediately. There are far better Battlefield games and shooters out there that actually run properly and have active player bases.

claims.claim: The game includes a solo and cooperative mode to play with and against AI bots in conquest and breakthrough game modes.

citations.review_text: Not as good as BF4 or BF3, which were the best with the best maps. The damage you have to inflict to enemies is too much, especially with vehicles. Having to re equip your gun loadouts each time you start a new game is annoying, if I choose a certain loadout why do I need to choose it again in game? Unneccesary and frustrating mechanics. The death cam after dying and having to skip it each time is also frustrating. There should be an AI mode with all game modes, and not only breakthrough and conquest, so that you can play all modes offline without having to join servers, especially for players from countries that lag a lot due to no available servers close to them. Shooting vehicle weapons from the weapons seats dont have good mechanics at all, and slight movement of the vehicle throws you off completely. Otherwise good game. The singleplayer should just have been longer seeing as online is basically dead, especially for the price - because its unplayable after the singeplayer and AI mode on only conquest and breakthrough gets boring.

Currently the best Battlefield single-player experience you can have. Reminds me of the days I spent playing battefield Vietnam and Battlefield 2. Tons of AI bots running around, flying planes and driving tanks and just massive battles were you feel like just another grunt, it's beautiful. You won't find this kind of solo play in battlefield 6, sadly.

So, unlike other reviews, I'm not going to bother critiquing the graphics and game mechanics because, well, they are AAA material.  Most negative comments come from the multiplayer crowd (MP as in human vs human) and players who can't take their time and think things through or wait 2-5 seconds for something to happen.

To be clear, BF-2042 is certainly not perfect, but if on sale, it is definitely a good game despite the negatives.

The one thing Battlefield 2042 has going for it is the "Experience Building."  No, it's not map building in the true sense of the phrase.  It's more like creating scenarios with existing set of 8-25 maps/terrains for you and your buddies to play around in.  You can create cooperative scenarios where human players vs AI enemy (real coop, not multiplayer).  Or even a solo scenario where you join one of two teams made up of bots on certain maps (and subsequent weapons/equipment/characters) from Battlefield 2042, BF-3, BF-4, or BF-1942.

It might not be the best Battlefield in the series, but playing the full Conquest and Breakthrough modes with/against bots—with full weapon progression—is actually really fun.

The bots are surprisingly well-made: they repair vehicles, take cover with their vehicles if hit by a rocket launcher, heal the wounded, throw smoke on downed teammates before reviving them, destroy enemy vehicles, and actively use both aircraft and ground vehicles. Almost all of my playtime in this game was spent specifically in this mode against bots.

The only downside to the bot mode is that they get lost on some maps, and sometimes you can clearly see the game rigging enemy bot spawns to force your team into a loss, even when you personally get 300 kills a match.

But overall, playing with bots is a really fun gaming experience, and I was genuinely able to feel that signature Battlefield atmosphere in this mode. It feels incredibly epic. Also, it seems like you can play the bot mode not just solo but in co-op as well, though I haven't tested that feature. Playing solo is definitely a blast.

The game had a terrible launch, probably the worst in the franchise. But now it's mostly fixed and in a good state. The specialists were an interesting experemint, that brought some new interesting mechanics to the game. But sometimes seeing the same faces in your squad, was awkward and their voicelines are annoying, too. Vehicle gameplay is fine, I actually prefer the vehicles of BF 2042 to those of BF6.

Battlefield 2042 is one of the biggest turnarounds I've seen in gaming. At launch it felt unfinished, lacking many of the features and atmosphere that made Battlefield great. After years of updates, reworks, and fixes, the game is finally in a state where it can stand on its own. The gunplay feels solid, the maps have improved significantly, and those large-scale Battlefield moments—where everything descends into absolute chaos—are back. It's still not the strongest entry in the franchise, and some design decisions remain divisive, but it's a far better game than the one that released. However, a new battlefield has came to be.

Battlefield 2042 had one of the roughest launches in the series, but after a lot of updates, it’s honestly in a much better state now.
At its core, the game still delivers those classic Battlefield moments where absolute chaos happens everywhere at once - tanks exploding, helicopters crashing into buildings, entire squads pushing objectives together, and random nonsense somehow turning into cinematic moments.

The gunplay feels solid, movement is smooth, and large-scale battles can be genuinely fun once everything clicks. Portal mode is also a great addition because it lets players revisit older Battlefield content and create some completely ridiculous custom game modes.

That said, the game still carries a lot of problems that stop it from reaching the same level as older Battlefield titles like Battlefield 3, 4, or 1. The specialist system remains controversial, some maps still feel too open, and the overall atmosphere lacks the gritty military vibe that older games had.

The good:
- Large-scale battles can be incredibly fun
- Gunplay feels satisfying
- Movement and traversal are smooth
- Battlefield chaos is still entertaining
- Portal mode is a great feature
- Vehicle combat can be exciting
- Much improved compared to launch
- Weather events look impressive
- Crossplay support is useful
- Some maps and modes are genuinely fun now

The bad:
- Launch damaged the game’s reputation badly
- Specialist system feels less immersive than classic classes
- Some maps feel too empty and oversized
- Teamplay feels weaker than older Battlefield games
- Bugs and server issues still happen
- Vehicle balance can be frustrating
- Atmosphere lacks the gritty feel of previous games
- Destruction feels downgraded compared to older titles
- UI and menus are awkward
- Still doesn’t fully feel like classic Battlefield

Overall, Battlefield 2042 went from being a disaster to being a decent multiplayer shooter. It’s much more enjoyable now than it was at launch, but even after all the im…
